def: A fine-tuning method that freezes the pretrained weights and learns the update to each chosen matrix as a product of two thin matrices.
The small set of trainable parameters added to a frozen model, such as LoRA's A and B matrices, that can be saved, swapped or merged.
The inner dimension r of the two LoRA factors, which sets how many independent directions the update can use and how many parameters it costs.
A constant that scales the adapter's output by alpha divided by the rank, interacting with the learning rate to set the effective step size.
The smallest number of free parameters in which a fine-tuning task can still be solved well, found to be far below a model's parameter count.
The family of methods, including LoRA, adapters and prompt tuning, that adapt a model by training only a small number of added or selected parameters.
LoRA training on top of a frozen base model stored in 4-bit NormalFloat, with double quantisation and paged optimisers to cut memory.
A 4-bit number format whose 16 levels are quantiles of a normal distribution, matched to the bell-shaped distribution of pretrained weights.
Quantising the per-block scale factors themselves, which reduces the storage overhead of 4-bit weights from about 0.5 to about 0.13 bit per weight.
Optimiser state held in memory that can move between GPU and CPU on demand, so a short memory spike does not crash a run.
Adding the product of the LoRA factors, scaled, into the base weights so that the tuned model has the original architecture and no extra latency.
